claims.claim: Powell sits in the electrical-distribution path between generation/grid supply and large industrial/data-center loads; record orders and a >$400M data-center project indicate switchgear/electrical equipment is participating in the physical infrastructure bottleneck.

The causal thesis depends on converting project awards through manufacturing capacity and delivery execution; backlog is a demand signal, not realized value, so capacity, labor, components and project timing are successor bottlenecks.

risks.risk: Mega-order concentration and manufacturing throughput can turn a strong demand bottleneck into schedule or margin risk.

unknowns.unknown: Customer concentration and incremental margin on the largest data-center award remain undisclosed.

claims.claim: Record $2.4B backlog and 3.0x book-to-bill materially strengthen demand visibility, but backlog must not be equated with revenue or profit because large projects can be delayed, modified or cancelled and carry execution risk.

Current profitability remained strong as bookings accelerated, so there is no evidence-based basis to manufacture a present bearish contradiction; the practical falsifier is backlog conversion accompanied by schedule slippage, cancellation or material margin degradation.

risks.risk: Project concentration, lumpiness and capacity expansion create execution and margin sensitivity even with strong bookings.

unknowns.unknown: The evidence does not disclose the margin profile or customer identity of the >$400M data-center order.
